issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the provided solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object. This return-type mismatch creates a semantic and structural inconsistency: students following the problem/UML will implement/expect an int, while the solution (and its auxiliary StudentCount class) uses a custom wrapper type. This can lead to compilation/test mismatches and confusion about the expected return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return an int (summing inscribed and guest students) so it matches the UML and problem description; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to document and justify the StudentCount wrapper type (and include StudentCount in the UML), so the use of a custom type is intentional and clear to students.
